summary:
I've written the held patch as one commit, a2b38315, on branch 'pool' in the scratch clone (on top of 24b8d1b9), and exported it with format-patch. It changes AirBattle.cpp, AirBattle.h and mix.json and nothing else. I checked that it applies cleanly to 24b8d1b9.

It does two things. First, a pool of reusable sound voices for the one-shot takes on the air path, each voice with a generation number. Second, a cap on how many takes begin in one frame: far takes over the cap are carried to the next frame, and dropped only after waiting longer than a stated bound. With none of the new mix.json keys present, the scene behaves exactly as today. A test harness compared every call into the audio engine against 24b8d1b9 and found them identical, 487 of 487.

There is no Unreal on this machine, so nothing has been built in the engine. Instead, every changed function and block was compiled from its literal text against stand-in types, with both g++ and clang++ (-std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Werror). I then ran a logic test of the pool and the cap against a model of the audio engine: 88 checks, none failed, same output from both builds. The first Mac build still has to confirm the real compile and the engine behaviour I assumed below.

design:
**What counts as a one-shot.** The pool and the cap apply to every take laid by `Sound()`, and to `SoundAtEye()` when it is not a loop.
- Loops go through `Lay` exactly as before. That means the formation engines (`EngineSounds`, `bAutoDestroy=false`), the ridden engine and the far bed.
- The ridden engine and far bed are worth flagging: they go through `SoundAtEye(bLoop=true)`, which calls `Lay` with `bAutoDestroy` left at its default of true. So the patch decides what is a loop by `bLoop`, not by `bAutoDestroy`. Splitting on `bAutoDestroy` would have pooled them.
- With none of the new keys in the mix, `Sound` and `SoundAtEye` take their original code path unchanged.

**New types in the header** (all inside the class, not reflected):
- `FAirTake`: a take's voice as the scene keeps it — a weak pointer to the component, the pool slot, the slot's generation, and whether the take is held.
- `FVoiceTake`: per pool slot — generation, when its part ends (`CutAt`), whether it was laid as a far take, whether it is fading.
- `FTakeAsk`: everything `Lay` needs to begin a take, plus `CutAt`, whether it is near, its gun key, when it was asked, and whether its gun has stopped.
- Members: `UPROPERTY() TArray<TObjectPtr<UAudioComponent>> VoicePool`, `TArray<FVoiceTake> VoiceTakes` alongside it, and `TArray<FTakeAsk> HeldTakes`.
- `GunTakes` is now `TMultiMap<int32, FAirTake>`.

**What is never capped, delayed or stolen ("near").**
- The ridden aircraft's own takes (any one-shot from `SoundAtEye`).
- A `Sound()` within 300 m of the eye when asked.
- Any `BigMoment` take.
- Everything else is "far".

**The pool** (`air.voicePool.voices` V, `air.voicePool.components` M; V=0 means no pool):
- Components are made lazily with `NewObject<UAudioComponent>(this)`, with `bAutoActivate=false`, `bAutoDestroy=false`, `bIsUISound=false`, then `RegisterComponent()`. They are owned by the actor and never destroyed.
- A voice is free when `IsPlaying()` is false. A voice still fading is never reused until its fade has finished.
- On reuse, every per-take field is set again before `Play(From)`: `SetSound` (only ever on a stopped voice), volume, pitch 1, spatialisation, attenuation settings (or null), world location, and the priority override (cleared when priority is 0 or less).
- At most V voices may sound without fading. Past that, the new take steals the farthest far voice that is still 300 m or more from the eye at that moment, and the stolen voice fades over `air.limits.cutFade` (0.3 s).
- A far take may only steal from a far voice farther away than itself; otherwise it waits.
- A near take with nothing to steal is laid over the count.
- If all M components are busy: a far take waits, and a near take gets its own `CreateSound2D` voice (with a timer for its cut), exactly as before the pool. It is never held.

**Generations.** Every new take on a slot increments its generation. `VoiceOf(Take)` returns the component only while the generation still matches, otherwise null.
- `KeepGunTake` (the old "keep the still-playing takes" pruning), the muzzle move, GunStop's fade and the cut all go through `VoiceOf`/`FadeTake`.
- So nothing holding an earlier take can fade, move or count a voice that has since been given to another take.
- Unpooled takes (slot -1) use the weak pointer exactly as today.

**Cuts.** For pooled takes, the per-take world timer is replaced by a check once a frame in `TakesDue()`, which is called in `Tick` right before `PlayEffects` and has a `TRACE_CPUPROFILER_EVENT_SCOPE` (`AirBattle_TakesDue`; `BeginTake` has one too).
- I chose this because it removes the timer churn too, and a stale cut cannot outlive a slot's reuse.
- The cut time is the start of the frame the take was asked in (world time minus that frame's delta) plus the cut, so the fade lands on the same frame the timer would have fired. This held in all three frame patterns tested, including 170/6 ms.
- Unpooled takes keep their timer.

**The cap** (`air.takesPerFrame` C; C=0 means no cap):
- `TakesBegun` counts every take begun this frame, near ones included.
- A far take finding the count at C, or finding no voice, is held. Near takes are never held.
- `TakesDue()` begins held takes oldest first, before any new take that frame.
- A held take that again finds no room is kept while it has waited no more than `air.takesHeldFor` (0.12 s; the code clamps it to 0.25 s, under the 0.3 s minimum gap between a gun's takes, so a gun has at most one take held). Past that it is dropped.
- So a held take begins at most 0.12 s plus one frame late: about 0.14 s at 60 fps, about 0.29 s on 170 ms frames.
- A held gun take is added to `GunTakes` when it begins and keeps its original cut time, so the gun's takes still run end to end.
- If its gun stops while it is held, it is still begun and then faded at once (0.08 s). That matches today's behaviour for a gun that fires for a single frame.

**Unchanged.** Levels and priorities are computed exactly as before. Ship batteries keep their `ShipGuns::HeardKey` keys.

**Logging.**
- `EndPlay` stops the pooled voices and clears the held takes.
- The mix numbers are read once in `Open`, with a log line when the pool or cap is on.
- The 20 s tally line ("takes laid on") gains, only when the pool or cap is on: "Voices: N takes pooled, voices made, reused, stolen; held, dropped (after X s); on a voice of their own." With both off it prints exactly as before.

**mix.json values** (each key has its note; the block has a `_note`):
- `air.voicePool.voices` 96: the engine's 128 voices minus about 30 for loops and music.
- `air.voicePool.components` 128.
- `air.takesPerFrame` 10.
- `air.takesHeldFor` 0.12.
apiAssumptions: There are no engine headers anywhere on this machine. I searched for AudioComponent.h, GameplayStatics.h and TimerManager.h across the filesystem; /home/user/air-r2 contains only the game's own source. Everything below is from memory of UE 5.x, and the harness's fake engine encodes it.

CreateSound2D creates a new UAudioComponent on every call (via FAudioDevice::CreateComponent: NewObject then register with the world), sets it as an interface sound with bAutoDestroy as passed, and leaves it unattached. Confidence: high (about 90%). Its outer (world settings or transient package) and bStopWhenOwnerDestroyed=false: medium (about 60%). The patch relies only on 'a new component per call' and sets every flag it needs itself.

UAudioComponent::Play while already playing stops the current sound dead (with auto-destroy suppressed during that stop) and begins the new one. Confidence about 80%. The patch never does this: it reuses a voice only when IsPlaying() is false, and the harness asserts zero plays on a playing voice across all tests.

SetSound while playing stops the sound and restarts it with the new one; on a stopped component it only assigns the sound. Confidence about 75% and 85%. The patch calls SetSound only on stopped voices.

FadeOut(D, 0) on a playing component fades it over D and then stops the sound, after which the component goes inactive. Confidence about 85%; today's GunStop and cut timers already rely on this. FadeOut on an inactive component does nothing (about 75%).

FadeOut followed by Play on the same component: Play clears the fading flag and stops the fading sound dead, which would click. Confidence about 75%. The patch never does this; a fading voice stays busy until IsPlaying() is false.

IsPlaying() stays true during a fade and becomes false only after the stop has been reported from the audio thread to the game thread, a frame or so after the sound ends. Confidence about 80%. The patch tracks fading itself (FVoiceTake.bFading) and does not use GetPlayState.

With bAutoDestroy=false a component stays registered and inactive after its sound ends or is stopped, and can be played again. Confidence about 90%. With bAutoDestroy=true (today's takes) it is destroyed at its end, and TWeakObjectPtr::IsValid/Get return false/null for it (about 90%).

OnAudioFinished is broadcast when a sound finishes (about 90%). The patch does not use it: it checks IsPlaying() when looking for a free voice, which avoids binding a delegate per take and any ordering question with the generation.

Late completions: UE 5.x keeps a per-component count of active sounds so a late completion from an earlier take does not deactivate a newer one. Confidence about 60%. The patch does not depend on this, since a voice is reused only after its last completion has arrived.

Pause: sounds with bIsUISound=false pause with the game; the actor does not tick while paused (bTickEvenWhenPaused is false by default); world timers do not tick; world time does not advance. Confidence about 80%. So the per-frame cut check and the old timer both wait out a pause the same way. Pooled voices are never SetPaused.

Timer timing: FTimerManager::Tick runs after the tick groups in UWorld::Tick, advanced by the frame's float DeltaSeconds; world TimeSeconds (a double) is advanced by the same delta before actors tick; UWorld::GetDeltaSeconds() returns that delta. Confidence about 75%. If this is right, the pooled cut time (TimeSeconds - DeltaSeconds + Cut) is reached on the same frame the timer would have fired; the harness confirmed it under this model with even, 170/6 ms and uneven frames.

Priority: the bOverridePriority/Priority values are read when Play is called, so they must be set before it. This is Lay's existing assumption (about 85%). A reused voice therefore has the override cleared when its new take's priority is 0 or less.

NewObject<UAudioComponent>(Actor) followed by RegisterComponent gives a component owned by the actor (through its outer), registered with the actor's world and audio device, and attached to nothing, so SetWorldLocation places it as with CreateSound2D's components (about 85%). bAutoActivate defaults to true for audio components, so it must be cleared before registering or a set sound would play (about 80%). Owned components are stopped on unregister when the owner goes, since bStopWhenOwnerDestroyed defaults to true (about 70%). EndPlay also stops them explicitly.
GC: the UPROPERTY TArray<TObjectPtr<UAudioComponent>> keeps the pooled components referenced, and they are also in the actor's owned components (about 95%).

The only per-component state a take leaves behind is sound, volume and pitch multipliers, attenuation settings, spatialisation flag, location and priority override; the patch resets all of them on reuse. Nothing else (low-pass filter, concurrency, parameters, envelope delegates) is ever set on a one-shot take. Confidence about 85%.

UnrealHeaderTool accepts non-reflected nested structs, and TWeakObjectPtr of forward-declared types, inside the UCLASS. Both patterns already exist in this header (FKeptLamp's TWeakObjectPtr<UDirectionalLightComponent>, and GunTakes' old TWeakObjectPtr<UAudioComponent>). Confidence about 90%.

The build's -Wshadow (UE5's default for shadowed variables) finds no new local named like a field of AActor or UObject; the new names are Here, Ask, Take, Level, Voice, Slot, Given, Waiting, Begun, Voices, Moving, Laid. Confidence about 85%; the stand-in base classes are small, so the real compile still has to confirm it.

tests:
Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f72655a4-7644-5fc7-a528-2e8434e56a4b/scratchpad/pool/check/pool_check_gcc and pool_check_clang: 88 checks, none failed, identical output from both. Logs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f72655a4-7644-5fc7-a528-2e8434e56a4b/scratchpad/pool/check/run_gcc.log and run_clang.log.

The test runs the literal patched code against a fake engine. That engine models play state, fades shortening a take's end, completions seen a frame late, auto-destroy invalidating weak pointers, world timers ticked after the scene, and frames with a float delta.

1. **Keys absent equals today.** The same scripted scene was run on the base code and on the patched code: far, near, own, out-of-earshot, missing-recording and whole-take guns; stops and restarts; a crack, a big moment, a delayed flak burst; loops; 170/6 ms frames. Result: 487 of 487 engine calls identical in order and arguments, the same counters, and a byte-identical tally line.
2. **Generations.** A gun's old handle to slot 0, after the slot was given to another gun's take, no longer reaches it. That gun's muzzle move did not move the other voice, its GunStop did not fade it, and the pruning dropped the stale handle.
3. **Cuts.** The per-frame cut landed on the timer's frame for 32/32 cuts at 1/60 s, 108/108 at 170/6 ms and 50/50 with uneven frames.
4. **Stealing.** A near take steals the farthest far voice, which fades over 0.3 s. A far take steals only a farther voice, otherwise it is held. Own takes and big moments steal but are never themselves stolen. A far voice carried to within 300 m is not stolen. With nothing stealable, a near take is laid over the count.
5. **Cap.** Held takes begin on the next frame, oldest first, ahead of new ones. Near, own and big takes are begun past the cap and counted. Drop bound: with a cap of 1 and 12 takes asked at once at 60 fps, 9 were begun (the last after 0.133 s, within 0.12 s plus one frame) and 3 were dropped, each only after waiting more than 0.12 s. On 170/6 ms frames, every take held on the long frame began on the short one.
6. **Held gun takes.** A held gun take is added to GunTakes when it begins, with its cut at the original time. A gun that stopped while its take was held still had the take begun, faded at once, and not kept. Takes-laid count is correct.
7. **Loops.** With the pool full and the cap full, the bed and drone loops still went through CreateSound2D with their old auto-destroy settings, were not pooled, and were not counted against the cap.
8. **Pool full and reuse.** With every component busy, a near take gets its own voice and a far take waits. A reused voice is fully reset: spatialisation, attenuation, priority override, volume, sound, owner, registration, auto-activate.
9. **Mix, EndPlay, tally.** Keys absent: no pool, no cap, no log line. Components default to 1.5 times voices; takesHeldFor clamps to 0.25. EndPlay stops pooled voices and clears held takes. The tally gains its Voices tail.
10. **Stress run.** 220 synthetic guns, 600 frames alternating 170/6 ms then 1,000 at 1/60 s, with the mix.json numbers:
   - 7,743 takes on 123 components (7,620 reuses); the old path would have made 7,743 components and their timers.
   - 80 stolen, 3,642 held, 130 dropped; at most 96 sounding.
   - Never a near take held, never a take left held past the bound, never a drop before the bound, never more than 128 components, never a Play or SetSound on a playing voice, and the TakesDue scope on every frame.

All of this tests the scene's bookkeeping against my model of the engine, not the engine itself.
openQuestions: With the pool on, pooled takes stop when the battle closes (EndPlay, and again when the actor's components unregister). Today's CreateSound2D takes play on to their end after the scene closes. The difference is only at teardown, and the end duck already has them about 10 dB down, but should they fade over cutFade instead?

The numbers 96 voices and 128 components assume the Mac's engine plays 128 voices and that about 30 go to loops and music. The existing log line 'the engine plays up to %d voices' and the formation count on the Bremen run should confirm this. At 32 voices the pool should be about 20.

The cap counts per frame, so on the stalled Mac (about 11 frames a second) it allows fewer takes per second than at 60 fps. In the synthetic stress run, 130 of about 7,900 far takes were dropped, mostly in the 170/6 ms stretch. The real figure will be in the tally's held and dropped counts.
Should a far take be allowed to steal a farther far voice (the analogue of the mix's explosionsYield rule), or should far takes only ever wait? The sound thread should say.
When a held gun take's gun stops before it begins, the patch still begins it and fades it at once (about 0.08 s), as a gun firing for one frame is heard today. Would the lead rather drop it?

A held take's cut is counted from when it was asked, so it plays shorter by its wait and the gun's takes still run end to end. Counting from when it actually begins would keep its full part but overlap the gun's next take by up to the wait. Takes that play whole (rifle-calibre mg42) can still overlap their successor by up to the wait.
The patch removes component creation and destruction, GC pressure and per-take timers. Each take's Play cost remains, bounded only by the cap. The Mac trace needs to show which of these dominates.

None of this has been compiled in Unreal: UnrealHeaderTool on the new nested structs, Mac clang's shadow warnings against the real AActor fields, and the engine behaviour assumed above all need the first Mac build and a run with the pool keys on. The Open log line and the tally's Voices tail are there to confirm the pool is actually running.

summary:
I reviewed a2b38315 for engine semantics and lifetimes. There are no engine headers anywhere on this machine: I searched the whole filesystem for AudioComponent.h, GameplayStatics.h, TimerManager.h and ActorComponent.h and found none. So every engine fact below is from memory of UE 5.0–5.5, and 5.8 itself can't be checked here.

One finding is major: the per-frame cut that replaces the world timer fires a frame early. The patch's "lands on the same frame the timer would have fired" rests on a wrong model of FTimerManager, and the author's harness encodes that same model, so its 108/108 result proves nothing. As I remember UE, a timer set during an actor's Tick goes to PendingTimerSet holding only its delay. At the end of that frame's timer tick, the delay is added to InternalTime, which already includes this frame's delta. It then fires on a strict `InternalTime > ExpireTime`. I'm about 80–85% sure of this.

I copied the harness to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f72655a4-7644-5fc7-a528-2e8434e56a4b/scratchpad/pool/review-ue-api/check and changed only its FTimerManager to that behaviour. The author's check 3 then fails:
- 0 of 32 cuts on the timer's frame at 60 fps
- 0 of 106 at 170/6 ms
- 10 of 50 with uneven frames

My own simulation (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f72655a4-7644-5fc7-a528-2e8434e56a4b/scratchpad/pool/review-ue-api/cutsim.py) agrees: every pooled cut is one frame early at 60 fps, 176 ms early for takes laid on a long Bremen frame, and up to 70 ms early with uneven frames. With the fix below, the harness gives 32/32, 106/106 and 50/50 (run_fixed.log). Its only remaining failure is pool_check.cpp:699, which hard-codes the old formula.

The other engine uses hold up:
- The actor has a root (AirBattle.cpp:536–537), so registering a component without one doesn't arise.
- Play and SetSound are only ever called on a voice that has stopped, and a fading voice is never played again.
- bAutoActivate is cleared before RegisterComponent.
- The priority override is set before Play and cleared again on reuse.
- Spatialisation, attenuation, volume and pitch are reset on every take, and bIsUISound is false, so voices pause with the game.
- The pool is kept from garbage collection by the UPROPERTY TArray and the actor's owned components.
- Pause behaves the same as before: the actor doesn't tick, world time doesn't advance, and timers don't tick.
- No other code keeps a returned component (the crack code only tests it as a bool), and no new local shadows an existing name.
- Replay actors are spawned fresh for each battle (CampaignGameMode.cpp:209), so Open running twice on one actor doesn't happen.

Two of the author's engine assumptions need correcting. First, CreateSound2D in 5.x makes its component with the context actor (this scene) as owner, so today's takes are already this actor's components and the pool doesn't raise the component count. Second, IsPlaying() is IsActive(): it stays true through a fade and through the delay before the audio thread's completion report reaches the game thread. That delay is what drives the second finding below.

findings.what: The per-frame cut assumes the wrong world-timer timing, so every pooled take is cut one frame early: 17 ms at 60 fps, 176 ms on the Bremen film's 170 ms frames, up to 70 ms with uneven frames. The claimed parity with the timer is false; the harness only agreed because its fake FTimerManager expires a timer at (time before this frame's advance + Rate) and fires on <=. As I remember UE 5.x (about 80-85% sure), FTimerManager::InternalSetTimer, when called before the manager has ticked this frame (which is the case from an actor Tick in TG_PostPhysics), puts the timer in PendingTimerSet with ExpireTime holding only the delay. At the end of FTimerManager::Tick it does `ExpireTime += InternalTime`, using this frame's already-advanced time, and it fires on `InternalTime > ExpireTime`. Under that behaviour the author's own check 3 fails (0/32 at 60 fps, 0/106 at 170/6 ms, 10/50 uneven). Since the next take of a burst is due only 0.02 s before the part ends, cutting a frame early opens a dip between takes once frames are uneven.
findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:6294 and :6384 (Ask.CutAt = Asked - GetDeltaSeconds() + Cut); :6649 (Now >= Take.CutAt); :6579/:6588 (FrameFrom = Now - Delta in the own-voice timer path); harness pool_check.cpp:699 and the FTimerManager stub in ue_pool_stubs.h:448-466
findings.fix: Count the cut from the frame's own time and drop GetDeltaSeconds: `Ask.CutAt = Cut > 0.0f ? Ask.Asked + Cut : -1.0;` in both Sound and SoundAtEye. In TakesDue fire on `Now > Take.CutAt` (strict). In BeginTake's own-voice fallback use `FrameFrom = Here->GetTimeSeconds()`, so the timer's ExpireTime becomes exactly CutAt; keep the Max(0.02, ...) floor, because SetTimer with a rate of 0 or less clears the timer. Make the harness timer pending (delay held, made absolute after the frame's advance, strict >) and change the expectation at pool_check.cpp:699 to asked time + 0.85. Verified in my copy of the harness: 32/32, 106/106 and 50/50 on the timer's frame. On the first Mac build, also log a handful of timer-cut and pooled-cut frame numbers side by side to confirm.

findings.what: The count of voices sounding, which decides when a far voice is stolen, depends on how late the engine reports a take's end. IsPlaying() is IsActive() in 5.x and goes false only when PlaybackCompleted reaches the game thread. The audio side notices a one-shot's end only at its once-per-game-frame update, and the completion is then sent to the game thread's task queue. So a voice whose take has ended still counts as sounding (and stays busy) for about 1-2 game frames, up to about 350 ms on the 170/6 ms pattern (about 70% sure). On exactly the frames the patch targets, audible far guns get stolen (faded) early, and far takes are held or dropped for lack of a free voice. The stress run's '96 sounding' used a one-frame delay model, not the engine's.
findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:6460-6466 (Sounding from IsPlaying and bFading); :6487-6498 (steal candidates)
findings.fix: Record when each pooled take should end (FVoiceTake::EndsAt): when begun, Asked + (Played->GetDuration() - From) for a whole take, or CutAt + 0.08 for one with a part; on a steal, Now + CutFade. Count a voice as sounding only while !bFading && Now < EndsAt. Keep IsPlaying()==false as the only test for reusing a voice. Add the number of voices sounding past EndsAt to the tally so the Mac run shows the real delay.

findings.what: The pool's numbers don't match how the engine counts voices. Every playing sound uses an engine voice, so up to PoolMost - PoolVoices = 32 fading pooled voices, near takes on voices of their own, and about 30 loops all count against MaxChannels, on top of the 96 sounding. Under load the engine still drops voices itself, by volume times priority and without a fade, which defeats the note's 'gives up a voice only where the engine would otherwise drop one'. And if the Mac still runs the engine's default 32 voices (the code's own comment at :741 allows for that), a pool of 96 never steals at all.
findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:769-772 (PoolVoices/PoolMost read with no reference to the device); :741-748 (Device->GetMaxChannels() already read just above); mix.json air.voicePool
findings.fix: In Open, after Device->GetMaxChannels(), clamp PoolMost to MaxChannels minus a reserve for loops (the most formation loops, plus the ridden engine, the far bed and the music) and keep PoolVoices at least the cutFade share below PoolMost. Log the clamped numbers next to the existing 'engine plays up to %d voices' line.

findings.what: With no audio (-nosound, GEngine->UseSound() false, World->bAllowAudioPlayback false, or no audio device), CreateSound2D returns null, so today such takes count as out of earshot or lost. The pooled branch still creates and registers a component, sets it up and calls Play, which does nothing (GetAudioDevice is null). It then returns the component, so the take counts in GunTakesLaid and TakesPooled. The tally that is meant to prove every gun was heard reports silent takes as heard, and a sound-off comparison run with the pool keys still in the mix pays per-take work.
findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:6517-6558 (pooled branch of BeginTake); :6325 (Sound returns VoiceOf(Take))
findings.fix: At the top of the pooled branch, mirror CreateSound2D: `UWorld* const W = GetWorld(); if (!GEngine || !GEngine->UseSound() || !W || !W->bAllowAudioPlayback || !W->GetAudioDevice().IsValid()) { return false; }`, or after Voice->Play check `if (!Voice->IsPlaying())` and treat the take as not laid.

findings.what: Teardown differs from today, and the open question's 'fade instead' wouldn't work as written. A UAudioComponent defaults to bStopWhenOwnerDestroyed = true, so when the destroyed actor unregisters its components, UAudioComponent::OnUnregister calls Stop(). Any FadeOut in EndPlay would therefore be cut dead a moment later, with or without the Stop loop. Today's takes play to their end because CreateSound2D sets bStopWhenOwnerDestroyed = false, and an active one-shot survives its component being destroyed (about 75% sure).
findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:6520-6524 (new component flags); :6043-6050 (EndPlay Stop loop)
findings.fix: For today's behaviour, set `Made->bStopWhenOwnerDestroyed = false;` when the voice is made and remove the Stop loop from EndPlay (keep HeldTakes.Reset()). If the lead wants a fade instead, use FadeOut(CutFade) with that same flag, so the fade isn't cut by OnUnregister.

findings.what: Voices are made lazily in the busiest frames. NewObject plus RegisterComponent is exactly the per-take cost the trace is meant to isolate, and with lazy creation the first raid's heaviest frames still make up to the cap plus near takes each frame until about 123 exist. The pooled run's trace will show creation cost in the very frames being compared.
findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:6517-6527
findings.fix: Make min(PoolVoices, PoolMost) voices in Open once the mix has been read (bAutoActivate=false, bAutoDestroy=false, bIsUISound=false, then RegisterComponent), add VoiceTakes to match, and keep lazy creation only above that up to PoolMost.

findings.what: An unplaced pooled take (the ridden aircraft's own guns, via SoundAtEye) keeps the world position of the voice's previous placed take, which can be kilometres away. CreateSound2D's components sit at the world origin. With bAllowSpatialization=false and no attenuation it isn't heard differently. Only a distance-based concurrency rule (for example StopFarthestThenOldest) would see the stale position, and no concurrency is configured in source, ini or the import scripts (the assets themselves aren't on disk to check).
findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:6547-6550
findings.fix: Always place the voice: `Voice->SetWorldLocation(Ask.bPlaced ? Ask.Where : FVector::ZeroVector);` so an unplaced take matches CreateSound2D's.

findings.what: The comment overstates what GunStop's fade does. A gun's take that was stolen (already fading to 0 over cutFade, 0.3 s) is not shortened by GunStop's FadeTake(0.08): in 5.x, UAudioComponent::AdjustVolumeInternal ignores a fade-out whose level is at or above the fader's current target (0 >= 0), about 65% sure. So a stopped gun's stolen take trails for up to 0.3 s. It's harmless, but the comment at :4623 promises a fade it may not get.
findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:4623-4629 (GunStop FadeTake); :6503 (steal FadeOut)
findings.fix: Either accept it and reword the comment ('a stolen take already fading keeps its cutFade'), or on GunStop call Stop() on a pooled voice whose VoiceTakes[Slot].bFading is true from a steal. Stop is safe here: the voice can't be reused until IsPlaying() is false, and Stop is not followed by Play.

summary:
I reviewed commit a2b38315 for bookkeeping. I worked only in my own clone at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f72655a4-7644-5fc7-a528-2e8434e56a4b/scratchpad/pool/review-bookkeeping/r2h; the author's clone is untouched and still at a2b38315. The exported patch matches the commit. I re-cut the harness inputs from the commit: they are byte-identical to the author's, and the author's 88 checks pass again.

My own tests run the literal code against the author's model of the engine. They are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f72655a4-7644-5fc7-a528-2e8434e56a4b/scratchpad/pool/review-bookkeeping/harness/review_check.cpp, with output in review_run.log beside it. Prototype fixes for the first, third and fourth findings below are in harness/fix/gen/new_takes_due.inc and harness/fix/gen/new_begin_take.inc, with output in harness/fix/review_fix_run.log. With those fixes my tests for them pass and the author's 88 checks still pass. All of this tests the scene's bookkeeping against a model, not the engine.

What I found correct:
- **Generations.** GunTakes pruning, the muzzle move, GunStop and the cut all reach a pooled voice only through VoiceOf, and the generation changes on every new take of a slot. The weak Voice field of a pooled take is never read. Cut timers capture only components that are not pooled. Sound()'s raw return is used only as a true/false test by the gun and crack callers.
- **Stealing.** A stolen voice keeps its generation, so only its own take's gun still moves or fades it, which is correct.
- **Cuts.** A slot's cut time is reset whenever the slot gets a new take, so an old cut cannot reach a new take.
- **Loops.** SoundAtEye with bLoop, EngineSounds through Lay with bAutoDestroy=false, OwnEngine and AirBed are unchanged and not counted against the cap.
- **Freeing voices.** Pooled voices free when IsPlaying() goes false. No recording is used both as a loop and as a one-shot: SoundOf only sets looping on the *_loop names.
- **Counters.** TakesPooled always equals made plus reused. TakesHeld and TakesDropped count each take once. GunTakesLaid is counted either when the take is asked or when it later begins, never both.
- **Keys absent.** That path is the same as today. With the cap on and the pool off, the cut timer fires where the old one did.

One thing that predates the patch and is unchanged: GunStop uses the ship's stream key, but ship battery takes are kept under ShipGuns::HeardKey, so GunStop never fades them. A held ship take is likewise never marked as stopped.

The main problem is the first finding below. With mix.json's numbers on the Mac's 170/6 ms frames, the same far guns are dropped on every round, so continuously firing guns are never heard. The tally cannot show this.

findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:4515 (GunHeardAt set before the take is asked), 6666-6691 (TakesDue retries held takes in the order asked and drops them at 6684-6691); mix.json:718-721
findings.what: The same far guns are dropped on every round, so a gun can go unheard for its whole burst, or for as long as it keeps firing. Why: GunHeardAt is advanced by the whole part (0.66-0.83 s) when a take is asked, so a dropped take leaves its gun silent until that time. Guns that asked on the same frame fall due again on the same frame, because RealT moves once a frame and they share the same gap. They also ask in the same effect order, and the oldest-first retry gives the same guns the last places every time. On the Mac's 170/6 ms frames a held take gets one retry, on the 6 ms frame, and can be dropped on the next long frame. So at most 30 far takes asked on one frame survive with takesPerFrame 10. Measured on the literal code with mix.json's numbers (review_check.cpp, R1 and R6): 40 far gunners opening together for a 0.5 s burst, 10 never heard. 40 firing continuously for 5 s, the same 10 never heard at all. 60 guns, 30 never heard. At 60 fps with a cap of 1, 12 guns: 3 never heard in 2 s. This breaks 'every gun seen firing is heard' for good, not as a one-off drop after the bound. The _takesPerFrame note's 'room for about 500 guns' assumes the asks are spread evenly across frames.
findings.fix: In TakesDue's drop branch, when a gun take is dropped and its gun is still firing (Ask.bGun && !Ask.bStopped), bring its due time back so it asks again on the next frame, out of step with the others: `if (double* Due = GunHeardAt.Find(Ask.GunKey)) { *Due = FMath::Min(*Due, RealT); }`. Prototyped in harness/fix/gen/new_takes_due.inc: no gun unheard in R1 or R6, and the author's 88 checks still pass. Also retry gun takes first, starting with guns that have no take playing in GunTakes, ahead of far flak, bombs and passes. Correct the _takesPerFrame and _takesHeldFor notes for 170/6 ms frames, where the carry-over is in practice one 6 ms frame.

findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:4532-4535 (the held branch counts nothing), 6688-6691 (only ++TakesDropped), 6694, 6794 (the tally line)
findings.what: The gun tally no longer accounts for every burst, so it cannot show whether every gun was heard. A gun take that is held and then dropped is counted only in TakesDropped, which it shares with flak, bombs, crumps and passes. GunBursts against GunTakesLaid + GunTakesLost + GunTakesFar no longer adds up. In R1 the line reads '40 bursts begun, 30 takes laid on, 0 that could not play, 0 out of earshot', with '10 dropped' in the Voices tail of every kind. Separately, line 6694 counts a held gun take whose recording is missing on retry as out of earshot instead of could-not-play.
findings.fix: Add GunTakesDropped, incremented when Ask.bGun in the drop branch, and print it in the gun half of the line, e.g. ', %d gun takes dropped by the cap'. Optionally also count bursts that stopped with no take ever begun. In TakesDue, count a held gun take whose Played is null as GunTakesLost, not GunTakesFar.

findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:6295 (bNear set once, when asked), 6666-6669 (retried with the old bNear and Where), 4547-4558 (the muzzle move does not update held takes)
findings.what: A far take held by the cap is never treated as near again. If the eye comes within 300 m of it while it waits, after a camera cut or a closing fighter, it is still capped and can be dropped. In R2, ten takes at 320-410 m with a cap of 1, and the eye then within 300 m of all of them: 35 frame-takes still held and one dropped. That goes against 'anything within 300 m of the eye is never capped or delayed'. A held gun take also begins at the muzzle position from the frame it was asked, up to about 0.3 s out of date.
findings.fix: In TakesDue, retry a copy of the take with `Try.bNear = Try.bNear || (Try.bPlaced && Eye && FVector::Dist(Try.Where, Eye->GetActorLocation()) < 300.0 * UnitsPerMetre)` (prototyped; R2 passes). In the muzzle-move branch, also set Ask.Where = At for HeldTakes entries with Ask.bGun && Ask.GunKey == SoundKey.

findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:6503-6505 (the steal)
findings.what: A stolen take is never cut. The steal sets VoiceTakes[Taken].CutAt = -1, so a take stolen less than about 0.22 s before its cut fades over the whole 0.3 s and plays its ground echo past the point where its cut would have ended it. In R3 the cut would have ended it at 0.93 s, but it sounds until 1.117 s. A steal should free the voice sooner, not later.
findings.fix: Keep CutAt when stealing. TakesDue then fades it again over 0.08 s at the part end, which shortens the steal's fade (prototyped in harness/fix/gen/new_begin_take.inc; R3 ends at 0.93 s). Alternatively, fade over FMath::Min(CutFade, FMath::Max(0.08, CutAt + 0.08 - Now)).

findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:6460-6466 (the Sounding count), 6491 (choosing a voice to steal)
findings.what: Voices whose take has already ended can still count as sounding. Until the audio thread's completion reaches the game thread (about a frame, longer on 170 ms frames), IsPlaying() stays true. Whole takes that end without a cut (mg42 rifle takes, flak bursts, crumps, passes, cracks) also have bFading false, so they count. That causes steals and holds the count did not need, and VoicesStolen comes out too high. In R4 only one of two takes was really sounding, yet a 3 s flak burst still playing was stolen. This assumes completion arrives at least one frame late; I am fairly but not fully sure of that.
findings.fix: Keep a per-slot EndsAt, set when the take begins to Now + (Played->GetDuration() - From) when the duration is finite and short, and to no later than CutAt + 0.08. On a fade or steal, lower it to Now + the fade length. Count a voice as sounding, and allow it to be stolen, only while Now < EndsAt. Keep IsPlaying()==false as the only test for a free voice.

findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:6566 (++TakesOwnVoice), 6517-6563 (the pooled begin path, compared with Lay and CreateSound2D)
findings.what: Two counts can differ from what actually played. (a) TakesOwnVoice is counted before Lay runs, so a near take whose Lay returns null is still reported as given a voice of its own. (b) With no audio device, -nosound, or world->bAllowAudioPlayback false, CreateSound2D returns null. Today that makes Sound return null, so a gun's take is counted out of earshot. The pooled path instead makes a component and calls Play, which I believe does nothing and leaves it inactive (about 70% sure). The take is then counted as pooled, reused and gun-laid. So a sound-off control run with these mix keys would report takes laid that never played.
findings.fix: Increment TakesOwnVoice only after Lay returns a component. At the top of the pooled branch, return false with bHeld unset when `!GEngine || !GEngine->UseSound() || !GetWorld() || !GetWorld()->bAllowAudioPlayback || !GetWorld()->GetAudioDevice().IsValid()`, as CreateSound2D does.

findings.where: AirBattle.cpp:765-768 (Open comment), mix.json:721 (_takesHeldFor), AirBattle.h FTakeAsk and pool comments
findings.what: The comments' claim that 'a gun has at most one take held' holds only while HoldFor plus one frame is under 0.3 s. That is a gun's shortest gap, measured on RealT, which moves at most 0.1 s a frame. The 0.25 s clamp with frames over 50 ms, or 0.12 s with a frame over 180 ms, allows two. GunStop's loop and KeepGunTake handle several held takes, so nothing breaks; the comments are wrong. The _takesHeldFor note's '0.29 s on the Bremen film's 170 ms frames' also does not match the 170/6 ms pattern: a take held on a long frame either begins on the next 6 ms frame or is dropped on the following long frame.
findings.fix: Correct the comments and the mix note. Or clamp HoldFor below 0.3 s minus the longest expected frame, if one held take per gun is meant to hold.

summary:
Verdict: with the chosen mix values, the patch changes nothing anyone hears. The cap and the pool never come into play: across 27 runs (Bremen, Oahu and Midway; 60 fps, 1/30 s and the Mac's 170/6 ms pattern; three eyes on Bremen) not one take was held, delayed, dropped or stolen, and every gun burst in earshot was heard. The problem is a design flaw that shows as soon as the limits are tighter: a dropped gun take is never asked for again, so a short burst can go completely unheard. The cap of 10 also never engages, so it does no work.

**How it was checked.** I built r2h's flight core (24b8d1b9 core, drop 8) and copied model-r2g's sim_v.cpp into `sim_pool.cpp` with the patch's pool and cap ported line for line: Sound, SoundAtEye, AskTake, BeginTake, VoiceOf, FadeTake, KeepGunTake, TakesDue, the GunStop marking of held takes, and the held-take cut times.
- The engine model: IsPlaying turns false one frame after a take ends; a voice of its own is gone at the same moment.
- Audio runs on the unclamped world clock (0.17 s on the Mac's long frame); the scene's clocks run on RealT clamped to 0.1.
- Eye: strategy as in model-r2g (`EYE=r2g MOUNT=twin`). I added a B-17 ride and a fighter ride (the film run's `-TheaterAirBattleRideHold`), and the flak guns that sim_v left out.
- With the pool and cap off, it reproduces sim_v exactly: 2077 takes, same breakdown.
- All of it is in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f72655a4-7644-5fc7-a528-2e8434e56a4b/scratchpad/pool/review-heard/model/`: `sim_pool.cpp`, built by `make_pool.py` from `poolsim.inc`; logs and per-frame CSVs (`*-pool.csv`) are in `out/`.

**Bremen per frame, mix values (96 voices, 128 components, 10 a frame, 0.12 s).** The columns are 60 fps / 1/30 s / 170-6 ms.

| Eye | Most takes begun in a frame | Most components made (most sounding at once) |
|---|---|---|
| Strategy | 4 / 5 / 6 | 29 (25) / 32 (26) / 22 (17) |
| B-17 ride | 4 / 4 / 7 | 30 / 32 / 23 |
| Fighter ride | 4 / 5 / 8 | 32 / 33 / 22 |

- Held, max delay, dropped and stolen were all 0 in every case.
- Oahu and Midway: at most 3–6 takes a frame, at most 12–30 components; nothing held or stolen.
- Takes on the ridden aircraft's own guns, within 300 m, or big moments: never held, delayed, dropped or stolen in any run, including the tightened ones below.
- Bursts in earshot heard: 1150/1150 at 60 fps, 1028/1028 at 1/30 s, 1082/1082 at 170/6 (strategy); 1146/1146 on the B-17 ride (106 of them the ridden plane's own); 387/387 on the fighter ride.

**r2h vs r2g take rates.** Taken over the fight (about 47–290 s), the rise the patch expected is not there:

| Pacing | r2h takes/s (total) | r2g takes/s (total) |
|---|---|---|
| 60 fps | 8.5 (2070) | 7.6 (1822) |
| 1/30 s | 7.75 (1847) | 11.05 (2242) |
| 170/6 ms (per scene second) | 8.5 | 8.2 |

- Both peak at 27–31 takes in one second and 4–8 in one frame.
- Gun effects did rise a little at 60 fps (523/s vs 488/s), but shared keys for a twin mount or a wing and the at-least-0.3 s gap between a gun's takes absorb the extra gunner windows.

**Tightened limits, to see what happens when the cap or pool does engage.**
- Cap 1 on the 170/6 pattern: 158 takes dropped and 69 of 1082 bursts never heard.
- Pool of 12 voices (16 components): 10 of 1150 bursts never heard. Pool of 6 (9 components): 150 of 1150.
- Cap 2 to 4: takes are held only into the next frame (at most 0.006 s on the 170/6 pattern), with no drops.
- The delay bound holds everywhere: worst delays 0.133 s (60 fps and 1/30 s) and 0.176 s (170/6).

**Engine headers.** None are on this machine, so this is a model of the scene's bookkeeping on assumed engine behaviour, not the engine itself.

**Bearing on the hold decision.** With at most 8 takes begun in a frame, take creation would have to cost about 20 ms per take to explain a 170 ms frame. Voice churn looks unlikely as the stall's cause, so it is right to keep the patch held until the trace shows it.

findings.what: A held gun take that is dropped is never asked for again, so a burst whose only take is dropped is never heard. This breaks the owner's rule that every gun seen firing is heard. PlayEffects moves GunHeardAt on by a whole part (about 0.83 s) when the take is asked, before it is begun. If TakesDue then drops it after HoldFor, the gun stays silent until its next take falls due. A burst shorter than one part is lost entirely. The 20 s tally cannot show this: TakesDropped lumps gun takes in with flak and other takes, and 'bursts begun' against 'takes laid' never reveals a burst with no take. At the mix values this does not happen on Bremen, Oahu or Midway. It appears as soon as the cap or pool engages: cap 1 on the Mac's 170/6 ms pattern left 69 of 1082 Bremen bursts unheard (154 gun takes dropped); a 12-voice pool left 10 of 1150 unheard at 60 fps; a 6-voice pool left 150 of 1150 unheard. Every unheard burst was far, but these are guns within the 1.5 km earshot that the owner's rule covers.
findings.where: unreal/TheaterCommand/Source/TheaterCommand/Battle/AirBattle.cpp:4515 (GunHeardAt.Add before the take begins), 4532 (held branch), 6684-6690 (the drop in TakesDue), 6787-6797 (tally)
findings.fix: Add `bool bFirst` to FTakeAsk. Set it in PlayEffects when this is the burst's first take (`!Due`, or GunTakes holds no live take for SoundKey). In TakesDue, before `++TakesDropped`: if `Ask.bGun && Ask.bFirst`, begin it anyway as a near take (`FTakeAsk Forced = Ask; Forced.bNear = true; if (BeginTake(Forced, Begun)) { ++GunTakesLaid; Ask.bStopped ? FadeTake(Begun, 0.08f) : KeepGunTake(Ask.GunKey, Begun); }`). That costs at most one extra take per new burst. For a later take of a burst that is dropped, set `GunHeardAt.Add(Ask.GunKey, RealT)` so the gun asks again on its next frame instead of falling silent for a whole part. Add GunTakesDropped and BurstsNeverHeard counters to the 'takes laid on' tally so the Mac's log can confirm the owner's rule.

findings.what: The cap (air.takesPerFrame 10) never engages, so it holds nothing and removes no per-frame work. The most takes begun in one frame were 4 at 60 fps, 5 at 1/30 s and 6-8 on the 170/6 pattern on Bremen (strategy, B-17 ride, fighter ride), and 3-6 on Oahu and Midway. The `_takesPerFrame` note says 'it bites on the frame after a long one'; the model does not bear that out (the worst long frame had 8). The patch's premise that r2h's true-scale raids raise the take rate does not hold either: r2h ran 8.5 takes/s against r2g's 7.6 at 60 fps, 7.75 against 11.05 at 1/30 s, and 8.5 against 8.2 per scene second at 170/6. Peaks are 27-31 takes a second and at most 8 a frame for both. Takes the cap holds this way are delayed, not dropped. But the room between a cap that does nothing and one that silences guns is narrow: cap 2-4 only holds takes into the next 6 ms frame, while cap 1 drops 158 takes.
findings.where: unreal/TheaterCommand/Content/Data/Sound/mix.json:718-719 (takesPerFrame, _takesPerFrame); AirBattle.cpp:6449
findings.fix: Rewrite `_takesPerFrame` with the measured peaks: at most 4/5/8 takes a frame at 60 fps, 1/30 s and 170/6, so 10 is a safety net that never engages on Bremen, Oahu or Midway. If the lead wants the cap to do something, 4 holds 33 Bremen takes on the 170/6 pattern by one 6 ms frame, with no drops and no unheard burst. Never set it below 2. Base the ship decision on the pool alone.

findings.what: The pool sizes (96 voices, 128 components) are 3-4 times what the battles use: at most 28 sounding and 33 components made across all 27 runs. The 96 also contradicts the mix's own budget, limits.worldTotal = 64: '64 one-shots with the engine loops, the beds and the music stay under about 90 of the 128'. At 96 pooled one-shots plus loops, bed, music and near takes on voices of their own, the engine reaches its 128-voice limit and stops voices dead before the pool would fade one. That is the opposite of what `_voices` claims ('gives up a voice only where the engine would otherwise drop one, and fades it where the engine would stop it dead').
findings.where: unreal/TheaterCommand/Content/Data/Sound/mix.json:712-716 (voicePool.voices, _voices, components)
findings.fix: Set voices 64 and components 96, citing limits.worldTotal in the note. I re-ran Bremen with 64/96 at 60 fps, 1/30 s and 170/6, strategy and fighter ride: identical results, nothing held, stolen or dropped, at most 22-33 components made.

findings.what: Taking a voice ignores what kind of take is on it. A far gun take, or a far flak burst played after its delay, can take the voice of a 'plane lost' far take: explosion_far_01/02, which replaces plane_explode beyond 150 m and is not a big moment. That goes against air.limits.explosionsYield: 'A plane lost never gives way to a flak burst; a new flak burst can push out only a farther flak burst'. It does not happen at the mix values; with a 12-voice pool, 2 plane_explode voices were taken.
findings.where: unreal/TheaterCommand/Source/TheaterCommand/Battle/AirBattle.cpp:6484-6506 (the search for a voice to take); mix.json:704-705
findings.fix: Add `bool bKeep` to FVoiceTake, set when the take comes from a FxKind::Sound plane event (plane_explode, plane_down, or their explosion_far_0x stand-ins), and skip bKeep voices when choosing one to take. Pass the take's name in FTakeAsk. A take whose name is in air.limits.explosionsYield may then take only a voice whose take is also in that list.

findings.what: With the pool on, EndPlay stops every pooled voice dead, so takes sounding when the battle closes are cut off with a click. Today's CreateSound2D takes play out. Both settings below are from memory (no engine headers here), about 70% sure: CreateSound2D sets bStopWhenOwnerDestroyed=false and bIgnoreForFlushing=true. The pooled components are created with the defaults (stop with their owner, flushed at level change). This changes what is heard only at teardown.
findings.where: unreal/TheaterCommand/Source/TheaterCommand/Battle/AirBattle.cpp:6041-6050 (EndPlay Stop loop), 6516-6521 (NewObject/RegisterComponent)
findings.fix: At creation, set `Made->bStopWhenOwnerDestroyed = false; Made->bIgnoreForFlushing = true;`, as CreateSound2D's components have. In EndPlay, leave playing voices to finish (or `FadeOut(CutFade, 0.0f)`) instead of `Stop()`, and stop only voices that are not playing.

findings.what: Whether a take counts as near is fixed when it is asked, and a held take keeps the muzzle position from that moment. If a held far gun take's fighter closes inside 300 m while it waits, it is still treated as far and can be held again or dropped. That breaks 'anything within 300 m never delayed' for takes asked at about 300-320 m: a fighter covers 15-20 m in the 0.12 s wait.
findings.where: unreal/TheaterCommand/Source/TheaterCommand/Battle/AirBattle.cpp:6295 (bNear computed once), 6449 (cap test), 4633 (held asks touched only at GunStop)
findings.fix: In BeginTake, recompute `const bool bNear = Ask.bNear || (Ask.bPlaced && Eye && FVector::Dist(Ask.Where, Eye->GetActorLocation()) < 300.0 * UnitsPerMetre);` and use it in the cap, room and take-a-voice tests. On a Gun effect for a key whose take is held, update `Ask.Where = At` in HeldTakes, the same way the GunStop loop marks them.

findings.what: The `_takesHeldFor` note says a held take begins at most 0.29 s late on the Bremen film's 170 ms frames. On the Mac's actual alternating 170/6 ms frames, the worst measured delay is 0.176 s: a held take is retried on the 6 ms frame, then on the next 170 ms one. The 0.29 s figure applies only to back-to-back 170 ms frames. At 60 fps the measured bound is 0.133 s (the note says 0.14).
findings.where: unreal/TheaterCommand/Content/Data/Sound/mix.json:721
findings.fix: Reword to '0.13 s at 60 frames a second; about 0.18 s on the Bremen film's alternating 170/6 ms frames, 0.29 s at worst on back-to-back 170 ms frames'.
